questions.q: If a submarine is at -50 metres and it descends another 20 metres, what is the expression to find its new depth?
questions.a: The expression is (-50) + (-20). A student who answers (-50) + (+20) likely confuses "descending" (a negative change) with the distance value itself, failing to assign the correct sign to the movement.

questions.q: Explain why -5 degrees is colder than -2 degrees using the idea of a number line or a thermometer.
questions.a: -5 is colder because it is further to the left of zero on the number line. A student who says -5 is "bigger" because 5 is bigger than 2 is ignoring the negative sign, which indicates a position below the reference point of zero.

questions.q: A bank account has a balance of ₹100. You make a withdrawal (a debit) of ₹150. What is your new balance, and how do you represent it?
questions.a: The balance is -₹50. Steps: 1. Identify starting balance (+100). 2. Identify movement (-150 for withdrawal). 3. Expression: (+100) + (-150) = -50. A student who calculates 150 - 100 = 50 ignores the direction of the transaction (a loss from a smaller amount).

questions.q: If you are at floor -3 and you reach floor +2, what was the movement? Compare your result to the target.
questions.a: The movement was +5 floors. Expression: Target - Start = Movement, so (+2) - (-3) = +5. A student who answers -1 likely added the numbers incorrectly or failed to realize that subtracting a negative is the same as adding a positive (moving toward the positive direction).

questions.q: Critique the statement: "Subtracting a negative number always makes the result smaller."
questions.a: This is false. Subtracting a negative number is equivalent to adding a positive number, which makes the result larger. A student who thinks it makes the result smaller is likely treating the two minus signs as a single negative outcome rather than an inverse operation.

questions.q: Create a real-world scenario involving a temperature change that results in a final value of 0 degrees Celsius.
questions.a: A good response would be: "The temperature started at -4 degrees and rose by 4 degrees." A poor response would involve non-integer values or fail to demonstrate the "inverse" relationship needed to reach zero.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Problem solving with integers involves using positive and negative numbers to represent real-world changes, such as gains/losses, ______ above/below zero, or movements in a building or mine.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are in an elevator in a ______ that has floors below ground level.
Fill in the blank: If you then go up five floors, you add (+______) to your position.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to translate a word problem into an integer expression, correctly apply addition or subtraction based on the context (direction of movement), and identify the final position on a number line.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you are in an ______ in a building that has floors below ground level.
